Machine learning classification of DNA sequences

Source: R/classify.R
rb_classification.Rd

Functions to extract sequence features, train a Random Forest classifier, and predict marker types for unknown sequences based on sequence composition.

  • rb_sequence_features(): Extracts numerical features (length, GC/AT content, GC/AT skew) from DNA sequences.

  • rb_train_classifier(): Trains a Random Forest model to classify sequences into marker types using the tidymodels framework.

  • rb_classify_sequences(): Predicts marker types for new sequences using a trained model, applying confidence and length filtering.

Usage

rb_sequence_features(sequence)

rb_train_classifier(
  data,
  label_col = "seq_type",
  features = c("length", "gc_content", "at_content", "gc_skew", "at_skew"),
  trees = 500,
  mtry = 3,
  min_n = 5,
  prop = 0.8,
  seed = 123
)

rb_classify_sequences(
  model_result,
  data,
  confidence_threshold = 0.8,
  min_length = 100,
  sequence_col = "sequence",
  fallback_label = "other"
)

Arguments

sequence

A character vector of DNA sequences.

data

A data frame containing the sequences and/or features.

label_col

The name of the column in data containing the class labels (e.g., marker types like "12S", "COI").

features

A character vector of column names to use as predictor features.

trees

The number of trees in the Random Forest.

mtry

The number of predictors randomly sampled at each split.

min_n

The minimum number of data points in a terminal node.

prop

The proportion of data to use for the training set (the rest is used for testing).

seed

Random seed for reproducibility of the train/test split.

model_result

The output list from rb_train_classifier().

confidence_threshold

Minimum prediction probability required to confidently assign a class.

min_length

Minimum sequence length (in base pairs) required for classification.

sequence_col

The name of the column in data containing the raw sequences.

fallback_label

The label assigned when a sequence is too short or falls below the confidence_threshold (default "other").

Value

  • rb_sequence_features() returns a data frame of computed features (length, gc_content, at_content, gc_skew, at_skew).

  • rb_train_classifier() returns a list with elements: model (fitted workflow), metrics (yardstick metrics or NULL), test_results (test set predictions), conf_matrix (confusion matrix or NULL), label_col, and features.

  • rb_classify_sequences() returns the input data augmented with predicted_class, confidence_score, final_type, and prediction_source columns.

Details

These functions require the tidymodels packages (parsnip, recipes, rsample, yardstick, workflows) and the ranger engine. Install them with install.packages('tidymodels') and install.packages('ranger').

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Extract features
features <- rb_sequence_features(refs$sequence)
features$seq_type <- refs$seq_type

# Train classifier
model <- rb_train_classifier(features, label_col = "seq_type")
model$metrics

# Classify unknown sequences
predictions <- rb_classify_sequences(model, unknown_data)
table(predictions$prediction_source)
} # }
